# Introduction

Terrestrial wildlife populations play a fundamental role in ecosystem structure and function. Across taxonomic groups, wildlife contributes to key ecological processes such as nutrient cycling, energy flow, seed dispersal, trophic interactions, and habitat modification, thereby supporting biodiversity and strengthening ecosystem resilience (*Dirzo et al., 2014*). However, these populations are increasingly exposed to anthropogenic pressures, especially habitat alteration and land-use change, which may affect their distribution and abundance across space and time (*Newbold et al., 2015*). Understanding and monitoring these responses is therefore crucial for conservation planning, effective protected-area management, and evidence-based decision-making (*Coad et al., 2015*).

To better understand and monitor these responses, camera trapping has become a cost-effective, reliable, and non-invasive method for monitoring wildlife populations. By automatically capturing images or videos when animals move through the detection zone of infrared sensors, camera traps generate robust information on species occurrence, habitat use, activity patterns, and relative abundance while minimizing observer-related disturbance. Consequently, camera-trap data have become an important source of biodiversity information and are widely applied in ecological research, biodiversity monitoring, and adaptive conservation management (*Kays et al., 2009*). These data are valuable to both scientists and practitioners, as they support ecological analyses, advance understanding of species ecology, and provide critical insights into population status and trends (*O’Connell et al., 2011*).

```{r introduction_intro, echo=FALSE, results="asis", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

cat(object$reportTextElements$CT_Project$Intro_text, "\n\n")

focus_label <- .pretty_label(object$setting$focus_groups)

if (is.null(focus_label) || length(focus_label) == 0 || is.na(focus_label) || !nzchar(focus_label)) {
  focus_label <- "wildlife"
}

if (is.logical(object$info$is.EOW) && object$info$is.EOW) {
  cat("The [European Observatory of Wildlife (EOW)](https://wildlifeobservatory.org/) is a standardized camera-trapping network operating across more than 100 study areas in Europe. It is coordinated by the [ENETWILD](https://enetwild.com/) consortium and funded by the [European Food Safety Authority (EFSA)](https://www.efsa.europa.eu/en). Images collected by camera traps within this network are processed and archived in Agouti, exported in the [Camtrap-DP](https://camtrap-dp.tdwg.org/) standard format, and included in annual monitoring reports submitted to [EFSA](https://www.efsa.europa.eu/en). A key feature of the EOW protocol is the use of the [Random Encounter Model (REM)](https://github.com/MarcusRowcliffe/camtrapDensity) to estimate population density from camera-trap detections (Rowcliffe et al., 2014). As a result, the entire workflow follows an established and standardized framework.\n\n")
}

  "**. The aim is to estimate and monitor **",

))
```

# Methods

## Study Area

The study was conducted in Suivi Ratons Anlier, located in Belgium. The site is geographically defined by the coordinates 49.733°–49.781°N and 5.642°–5.716°E and covers an area of approximately 26.79 km².   The site supports a diverse range of wildlife, with approximately 49 species recorded. The most frequently observed species include *Cervus elaphus*, *Capreolus capreolus*, *Sus scrofa*, *Vulpes vulpes*, and *Apodemus sylvaticus*.

## Sampling

## Camera Locations {.tabset}

The maps below display the locations of camera traps deployed during different years. Use the tabs above to explore data for each sampling year. The last tab shows the study area with all camera locations in this site. Locations are color-coded by habitat type. Click on the points for additional deployment information.

```{r location_camera_locations_leaflet, echo = FALSE, results = 'asis', fig.show = "hold"}

# High-contrast categorical colours for habitat classes
.nice_habitat_palette <- function(n) {
  base_cols <- c(
    "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7",
    "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#882255", "#117733",
    "#332288", "#AA4499", "#44AA99", "#999933",
    "#661100", "#6699CC", "#AA4466", "#DDCC77",
    "#88CCEE", "#000000"
  )
  
  if (n <= length(base_cols)) {
    base_cols[seq_len(n)]
  } else {
    grDevices::hcl.colors(n, palette = "Dark 3")
  }
}

# Clean popup values: removes leading/trailing commas, repeated commas, and empty values
.popup_value <- function(x, missing = "No Data") {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x[is.na(x)] <- ""
  x <- gsub("^\\s*,+\\s*", "", x)
  x <- gsub("\\s*,+\\s*$", "", x)
  x <- gsub("\\s*,\\s*,+", ", ", x)
  x <- gsub("\\s+", " ", x)
  x <- trimws(x)
  ifelse(nzchar(x), htmltools::htmlEscape(x), missing)
}

# Function to plot camera locations with popups
plot_locations <- function(data, color_palette, add_legend = object$setting$locationLegend, .all_habitat) {
  
  if (is.null(data) || nrow(data) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  habitat_colors <- leaflet::colorFactor(
    palette = color_palette,
    domain = .all_habitat,
    na.color = "#1C1C1C"
  )
  
  data <- data |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      popup_text = paste0(
        "<b>Location:</b> ", .popup_value(locationName, "N/A"), "<br>",
        "<b>Habitat Type:</b> ", .popup_value(Habitat_Type, "N/A"), "<br>",
        "<b>Bait Use:</b> ", .popup_value(BaitUse_List), "<br>",
        "<b>Camera Height:</b> ", .popup_value(cameraHeight), "<br>",
        "<b>Species Observed:</b> ", .popup_value(Species_List), "<br>",
        "<b>Capture Method:</b> ", .popup_value(CaptureMethod_List), "<br>",
        "<b>Number of Photos:</b> ", .popup_value(Total_Photos), "<br>",
        "<b>Classified By:</b> ", .popup_value(Classify_By_List), "<br>",
        "<b>Setup By:</b> ", .popup_value(Setup_By_List)
      )
    )
  
  map <- leaflet::leaflet(data, width = "100%", height = "400px") |>
    leaflet::addTiles()
  
  if (!is.null(object$study_area) && !is.null(object$study_area$path)) {
    object$study_area$object <- terra::readRDS(object$study_area$path)
    .tmpStudyArea <- terra::project(object$study_area$object, "epsg:4326")
    
    map <- map |>
      leaflet::addPolygons(
        data = .tmpStudyArea,
        fillColor = "transparent",
        fillOpacity = 0.3,
        color = "black",
        weight = 2
      )
  }
  
  map <- map |>
    leaflet::addCircleMarkers(
      lng = ~longitude,
      lat = ~latitude,
      radius = 6,
      color = ~habitat_colors(Habitat_Type),
      fillOpacity = 0.85,
      stroke = TRUE,
      weight = 1,
      popup = ~popup_text
    ) |>
    leaflet::fitBounds(
      lng1 = min(data$longitude, na.rm = TRUE),
      lat1 = min(data$latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
      lng2 = max(data$longitude, na.rm = TRUE),
      lat2 = max(data$latitude, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  
  if (isTRUE(add_legend)) {
    map <- map |>
      leaflet::addLegend(
        position = "bottomright",
        pal = habitat_colors,
        values = .all_habitat,
        title = "Habitat Type",
        opacity = 1
      )
  }
  
  map
}

# Shared habitat domain for consistent colours across all tabs
.all_habitat <- unique(object$data_merged$Habitat_Type)
.all_habitat <- sort(.all_habitat[!is.na(.all_habitat) & .all_habitat != ""])
.habitat_palette <- .nice_habitat_palette(length(.all_habitat))

# Automatically create tabs for each year
for (doyear in object$years) {
  cat(paste0("### ", doyear, " {.unnumbered}\n\n"))
  
  .dat_year <- object$data_merged[
    object$data_merged$Year == doyear,
    c(
      "locationName", "cameraHeight", "BaitUse_List", "Species_List",
      "CaptureMethod_List", "Total_Photos", "Classify_By_List",
      "Setup_By_List", "longitude", "latitude", "Year", "Habitat_Type"
    )
  ]
  
  .dat_year <- .dat_year[
    !is.na(.dat_year$longitude) &
      !is.na(.dat_year$latitude),
  ]
  
  if (nrow(.dat_year) > 0) {
    p <- plot_locations(
      data = .dat_year,
      color_palette = .habitat_palette,
      .all_habitat = .all_habitat
    )
    print(htmltools::tagList(p))
  } else {
    cat(paste0("⚠️ No location data available for ", doyear, ".\n"))
  }
  
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Sampling Efforts

Sampling effort refers to the total number of camera trap operational days, accounting for both the number of active cameras and their duration of deployment. It provides critical context for interpreting species detection rates and comparing data across years. A summary of yearly sampling effort is provided below, including camera breakdowns, average operational days, and total effort per year:

```{r effort_camera_locations_leaflet, echo=FALSE, results="asis", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}


.camera_summary_text <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(object$camera_stats)), function(i) {
  year <- object$camera_stats$year[i]
  failed_cameras <- object$camera_stats$failed_cameras[i]
  average_runtime <- object$camera_stats$average_runtime[i]
  runtime_range <- object$camera_stats$runtime_range[i]
  total_runtime_days <- object$camera_stats$total_runtime_days[i]
  total_runtime_years <- object$camera_stats$total_runtime_years[i]

  broken_text <- if (failed_cameras == 0) {
    "No cameras broke down during the study period"
  } else if (failed_cameras == 1) {
    "One camera broke down during the study period"
  } else if (failed_cameras == 2) {
    "Two cameras broke down during the study period"
  } else {
    paste(failed_cameras, "cameras broke down during the study period")
  }

  paste0(
    "<p><strong>", year, ":</strong> ",
    broken_text,
    ", the cameras operated for an average of ", average_runtime,
    " days (range: ", runtime_range,
    " days), and the total sampling effort was ", total_runtime_days,
    " days, equivalent to ", total_runtime_years, " years.</p>"
  )
})
```

## Image Processing

To support standardized, reproducible, and interoperable workflows, camera-trap data are increasingly managed using dedicated platforms such as [Agouti](https://agouti.eu/) (*Casaer et al., 2019*) and structured according to community standards such as [CamtrapDP](https://camtrap-dp.tdwg.org/) (*Bubnicki et al., 2024*).
Agouti supports sequence-based annotation, AI-assisted classification, secure archiving, and standardized data export.
In this workflow, images recorded within 120 seconds of one another were grouped into sequences representing putative single events and annotated using a combination of AI-assisted classification and manual review; a subset was subsequently validated by experienced observers.
Where relevant for density estimation, calibration images and species-specific movement paths were also annotated and analysed using the photogrammetric tools in the R package [camtrapDensity](https://github.com/MarcusRowcliffe/camtrapDensity) (*Rowcliffe, 2014*).

```{r image_processing_image_processes, echo=FALSE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

cat("The images used in this report were processed and archived in ",
  object$reportTextElements$data_source,
  ", and the data were structured according to the CamtrapDP standard.","\n\n")
```

## Data Processing

The input data were provided in [Camtrap-DP standard format](https://camtrap-dp.tdwg.org/) and pre-processed in [camtrapReport](https://github.com/spatialecology/camtrapReport), including cleaning, harmonisation, organisation, summarisation, and extraction of key attributes. Records were checked for completeness and internal consistency before being summarised into the descriptive statistics and ecological metrics presented in this report. 

In the processing stage, ecological analysis modules operated on these standardised data to generate harmonised outputs, including tables, figures, text, and summary statistics. The report includes a broad range of ecological analyses, such as sampling effort, species richness, activity patterns, and species co-occurrence. These analyses draw on established ecological methods implemented in dedicated R packages, including [activity](https://github.com/MarcusRowcliffe/activity) and [camtrapDensity](https://github.com/MarcusRowcliffe/camtrapDensity). 

In the post-processing stage, outputs generated by the selected modules were assembled into structured report sections and rendered into a coherent, article-style ecological report. Because sections can be customised by the user, the report structure remains flexible and can be adapted to different study objectives. This workflow provides a reproducible and extensible framework for transforming raw camera-trap data into standardised ecological insights.

## Capture-Based and Abundance Trends {.tabset}

Camera-trap capture data do not directly measure true population size, but they can provide useful indicators of temporal variation in relative abundance and species detectability, provided that survey effort and detection conditions remain reasonably comparable among years.

```{r abundance_trends_abundance, echo=FALSE, results="asis", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=13.5, fig.height=7.5, out.width="100%", fig.align="center", dpi=150}

group_label <- .pretty_label(object$setting$focus_groups)

cat(paste0(
  "The figures below summarize capture-based trends for frequently detected ", group_label,
  " recorded in at least ", object$filterCount,
  " capture events during the study period in ", object$siteName, ". ",
  "The tabs present complementary metrics, including the number of captures, capture rate ",
  "(captures per 100 trap-days), number of capture locations, and, where available, ",
  "REM-based density estimates. Together, these metrics support comparison of temporal ",
  "patterns in species records across survey years.\n\n"
))

# -------------------------
# Helper functions
# -------------------------

.safe_mean <- function(x) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
  if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

.safe_sum <- function(x) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
  if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

.safe_max <- function(x) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
  if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

.make_species_colors <- function(species) {
  species <- unique(as.character(species))
  species <- species[!is.na(species) & nzchar(species)]
  
  n <- length(species)
  
  if (n == 0) {
    return(stats::setNames(character(0), character(0)))
  }
  
  if (n <= 6 && length(object$reportObjectElements$color_palette) >= n) {
    cols <- object$reportObjectElements$color_palette[seq_len(n)]
  } else {
    cols <- grDevices::hcl.colors(n, palette = "Dark 3")
  }
  
  stats::setNames(cols, species)
}

# -------------------------
# Survey-year axis helpers
# -------------------------

.make_year_axis <- function(years_all) {
  
  years_all <- sort(unique(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(years_all))))
  years_all <- years_all[is.finite(years_all)]
  
  gap_before <- c(FALSE, diff(years_all) > 1)
  
  data.frame(
    Year_numeric = years_all,
    Year_plot = seq_along(years_all),
    Year_label = as.character(years_all),
    gap_before = gap_before,
    Year_label_expr = ifelse(
      gap_before,
      paste0("bold('", years_all, "')"),
      paste0("'", years_all, "'")
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

.x_year_scale <- function(year_axis, expand_right = 0.30) {
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = year_axis$Year_plot,
    labels = parse(text = year_axis$Year_label_expr),
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.02, expand_right))
  )
}

.gap_caption_text <- function(year_axis) {
  if (any(year_axis$gap_before, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    " Bold year labels indicate a gap of more than one year since the previous available survey year."
  } else {
    ""
  }
}

.complete_species_years <- function(df, species_list, year_axis) {
  
  grid <- expand.grid(
    scientificName = species_list,
    Year_numeric = year_axis$Year_numeric,
    KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  grid |>
    dplyr::left_join(df, by = c("scientificName", "Year_numeric")) |>
    dplyr::left_join(year_axis, by = "Year_numeric") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Year = factor(.data$Year_label, levels = year_axis$Year_label)
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(.data$scientificName, .data$Year_plot)
}

.add_line_segments <- function(df, value_col) {
  
  df |>
    dplyr::arrange(.data$scientificName, .data$Year_plot) |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$scientificName) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      has_value_tmp = !is.na(.data[[value_col]]),
      previous_has_value_tmp = dplyr::lag(.data$has_value_tmp, default = FALSE),
      new_segment_tmp = .data$has_value_tmp & !.data$previous_has_value_tmp,
      segment_tmp = cumsum(.data$new_segment_tmp),
      line_group = ifelse(
        .data$has_value_tmp,
        paste(.data$scientificName, .data$segment_tmp, sep = "__"),
        NA_character_
      )
    ) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()
}

.latest_labels <- function(df, value_col) {
  
  df |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[value_col]])) |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$scientificName) |>
    dplyr::slice_max(order_by = .data$Year_plot, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()
}

.log10_labels <- function(x) {
  vapply(x, function(z) {
    
    if (!is.finite(z)) return("")
    
    if (z >= 1) {
      return(formatC(z, format = "f", digits = 0))
    }
    
    digits <- max(1, ceiling(-log10(z)))
    
    out <- formatC(z, format = "f", digits = digits)
    out <- sub("0+$", "", out)
    out <- sub("\\.$", "", out)
    
    out
    
  }, character(1))
}

.caption_html <- function(fig_no, text) {
  cat(paste0(
    '\n\n<p style="font-size:16px; color:black; font-weight:normal; margin-top:10px;">',
    '<b>Figure ', fig_no, '.</b> ',
    '<i>', text, '</i></p>\n\n'
  ))
}

.main_plot_theme <- function() {
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_family = "", base_size = 15) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", color = "black"),
      axis.title.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", color = "black"),
      axis.text.x  = ggplot2::element_text(size = 13, angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
      axis.text.y  = ggplot2::element_text(size = 13),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(22, 120, 22, 45)
    )
}

.facet_plot_theme <- function() {
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_family = "", base_size = 13) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
      axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", color = "black"),
      axis.title.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", color = "black"),
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()
    )
}

# -------------------------
# Species included in focus groups
# -------------------------

.w <- character()

if (!is.null(object$setting$focus_groups)) {
  .idx <- which(names(object$species_summary) %in% object$setting$focus_groups)
  if (length(.idx) > 0) {
    .w <- unlist(lapply(.idx, function(i) {
      object$species_summary[[i]]$site_list$scientificName
    }))
  }
}

if (length(.w) == 0) {
  if (any(c("wild_mammals", "large_mammals", "birds", "amphibians", "reptiles") %in% object$species_summary$count$Group)) {
    .idx <- which(names(object$species_summary) %in% c("wild_mammals", "large_mammals", "birds", "amphibians", "reptiles"))
    .w <- unlist(lapply(.idx, function(i) {
      object$species_summary[[i]]$site_list$scientificName
    }))
  } else {
    .w <- unique(object$capture$scientificName)
  }
}

.w <- unique(.w[!is.na(.w) & nzchar(.w)])

capture_base <- object$capture |>
  dplyr::filter(
    .data$scientificName %in% .w,
    .data$Year != "total",
    as.character(.data$Year) != "9999"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Year_numeric = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(.data$Year)))
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data$Year_numeric)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$scientificName, .data$Year_numeric) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Captures = .safe_sum(.data$Captures),
    Capture_Rate = .safe_mean(.data$Capture_Rate),
    Locations = .safe_max(.data$Locations),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$scientificName, .data$Year_numeric)

if (nrow(capture_base) == 0) {
  
  cat("\n\nNo capture data are available for the selected focus group.\n\n")
  
} else {
  
  species_list <- sort(unique(as.character(capture_base$scientificName)))
  years_all <- sort(unique(capture_base$Year_numeric))
  year_axis <- .make_year_axis(years_all)
  
  n_species <- length(species_list)
  many_species <- n_species > 100
  
  species_colors <- .make_species_colors(species_list)
  
  capture_plot_base <- .complete_species_years(
    capture_base,
    species_list = species_list,
    year_axis = year_axis
  )
  
  # -------------------------
  # Number of captures
  # -------------------------
  
  cat("### Number of Captures {.unnumbered}\n\n")
  
  capture_plot <- .add_line_segments(capture_plot_base, "Captures")
  
  if (many_species) {
    
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
      capture_plot,
      ggplot2::aes(
        x = .data$Year_plot,
        y = .data$Captures,
        group = .data$line_group,
        color = .data$scientificName
      )
    ) +
      ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1.1, na.rm = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE) +
      ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.8, shape = 21, fill = "white", stroke = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE) +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ scientificName, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
      .x_year_scale(year_axis, expand_right = 0.05) +
      ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = species_colors, drop = FALSE) +
      ggplot2::labs(
        x = "Survey Year",
        y = "Number of Captures"
      ) +
      .facet_plot_theme()
    
    print(p)
    
    .caption_html(
      object$getFigureNumber(text = FALSE),
      paste0(
        "Trends in camera-trap detections over the survey years for each study species in the ",
        group_label,
        " group, based on the number of captures. Species are shown in separate panels to improve readability.",
        .gap_caption_text(year_axis)
      )
    )
    
  } else {
    
    label_captures <- .latest_labels(capture_plot, "Captures")
    
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
      capture_plot,
      ggplot2::aes(
        x = .data$Year_plot,
        y = .data$Captures,

      )
    ) +
      ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1.5, na.rm = TRUE) +

      ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
        data = label_captures,
        ggplot2::aes(label = .data$scientificName),
        size = 4.2,
        nudge_x = 0.45,
        direction = "y",
        hjust = 0,

        segment.size = 0.4,
        box.padding = 0.35,
        point.padding = 0.25,
        family = "",
        show.legend = FALSE,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) +
      .x_year_scale(year_axis, expand_right = 0.30) +

        x = "Survey Year",
        y = "Number of Captures"
      ) +

    print(p)
    
    .caption_html(
      object$getFigureNumber(text = FALSE),
      paste0(

        group_label,
        " group, based on the number of captures.",
        .gap_caption_text(year_axis)
      )
    )
  }
  
  # -------------------------
  # Capture rate
  # -------------------------
  
  cat("### Capture Rate {.unnumbered}\n\n")
  
  df_capture_rate <- capture_plot_base |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      CaptureRate_100 = 100 * .data$Capture_Rate,
      CaptureRate_100 = dplyr::if_else(
        is.finite(.data$CaptureRate_100) & .data$CaptureRate_100 > 0,
        .data$CaptureRate_100,
        NA_real_
      )
    )
  
  df_capture_rate <- .add_line_segments(df_capture_rate, "CaptureRate_100")
  
  if (all(is.na(df_capture_rate$CaptureRate_100))) {
    
    cat("\n\nNo positive capture-rate values are available for plotting.\n\n")
    
  } else {
    
    min_rate <- min(df_capture_rate$CaptureRate_100, na.rm = TRUE)
    max_rate <- max(df_capture_rate$CaptureRate_100, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    y_lower <- if (is.finite(min_rate) && min_rate < 0.1) {
      10 ^ floor(log10(min_rate))
    } else {
      0.1
    }
    
    y_upper <- if (is.finite(max_rate) && max_rate > 100) {
      10 ^ ceiling(log10(max_rate))
    } else {
      100
    }
    
    y_breaks <- 10 ^ seq(log10(y_lower), log10(y_upper), by = 1)
    y_breaks <- y_breaks[y_breaks >= y_lower & y_breaks <= y_upper]
    
    if (many_species) {
      
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
        df_capture_rate,
        ggplot2::aes(
          x = .data$Year_plot,
          y = .data$CaptureRate_100,

          color = .data$scientificName
        )
      ) +
        ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1.1, na.rm = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE) +
        ggplot2::geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2.8, fill = "white", stroke = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE) +
        ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ scientificName, ncol = 3) +
        .x_year_scale(year_axis, expand_right = 0.05) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_log10(
          breaks = y_breaks,
          labels = .log10_labels,
          limits = c(y_lower, y_upper)
        ) +
        ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = species_colors, drop = FALSE) +

          x = "Survey Year",
          y = "Capture Rate per 100 trap-days"

        .facet_plot_theme()
      
      print(p)
      
      .caption_html(
        object$getFigureNumber(text = FALSE),
        paste0(
          "Capture rates per 100 trap-days are shown on a log10 scale for each study species in the ",
          group_label,
          " group across survey years. Species are shown in separate panels to reduce overlap.",
          .gap_caption_text(year_axis)
        )
      )
      
    } else {
      
      label_rate <- .latest_labels(df_capture_rate, "CaptureRate_100")
      
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
        df_capture_rate,
        ggplot2::aes(
          x = .data$Year_plot,
          y = .data$CaptureRate_100,
          group = .data$line_group,
          color = .data$scientificName
        )
      ) +
        ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1.5, na.rm = TRUE) +

        ) +
        .x_year_scale(year_axis, expand_right = 0.30) +

        ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = species_colors, drop = FALSE) +

      print(p)
      
      .caption_html(

  # -------------------------

  cat("### Number of Locations {.unnumbered}\n\n")
  
  location_plot <- .add_line_segments(capture_plot_base, "Locations")
  
  if (many_species) {
    
    species_order <- capture_base |>

    heat_data <- capture_plot_base |>

    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(

      ggplot2::geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +

        high = "#2C3E50",

        x = "Survey Year",

      ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +

    print(p)
    
    .caption_html(

  } else {
    
    label_locations <- .latest_labels(location_plot, "Locations")

    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(

        family = "",
        nudge_x = 0.45,
        hjust = 0,

        box.padding = 0.35,

      ) +
      .x_year_scale(year_axis, expand_right = 0.30) +
      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(

      ) +
      ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = species_colors, drop = FALSE) +

    print(p)
    
    .caption_html(
      object$getFigureNumber(text = FALSE),
      paste0(
        "Trends in the number of camera-trap locations where each species was recorded in the ",
        group_label,
        " group across survey years.",
        .gap_caption_text(year_axis)
      )
    )
  }
  
  # -------------------------
  # REM-based density
  # -------------------------
  
  cat("### REM-Based Density {.unnumbered}\n\n")
  
  spn <- object$get_speciesNames(object$setting$focus_groups)
  spn <- unique(spn[!is.na(spn) & nzchar(spn)])
  
  rem_list <- list()
  
  if (length(spn) > 0) {
    for (sp in spn) {
      tmp <- try(object$get_REM(sp), silent = TRUE)
      
      if (!inherits(tmp, "try-error") && !is.null(tmp) && length(tmp) > 0) {
        tmp_df <- try(dplyr::bind_rows(tmp), silent = TRUE)
        
        if (!inherits(tmp_df, "try-error") && is.data.frame(tmp_df) && nrow(tmp_df) > 0) {
          rem_list[[sp]] <- tmp_df
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  estimates_rem <- dplyr::bind_rows(rem_list)
  
  if (nrow(estimates_rem) == 0) {
    
    cat("\n\nREM-based density estimates are not available for the selected species.\n\n")
    
  } else {
    
    density_data <- estimates_rem |>
      dplyr::filter(.data$Metric == "density") |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        Year_numeric = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(.data$Year))),
        estimate = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data$estimate))
      ) |>
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(.data$Year_numeric),
        as.character(.data$Year) != "9999",
        is.finite(.data$estimate)
      ) |>
      dplyr::group_by(.data$scientificName, .data$Year_numeric) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        estimate = .safe_mean(.data$estimate),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
    
    if (nrow(density_data) == 0) {
      
      cat("\n\nAnnual REM-based density estimates are not available for plotting.\n\n")
      
    } else {
      
      rem_species <- sort(unique(as.character(density_data$scientificName)))
      rem_years <- sort(unique(density_data$Year_numeric))
      rem_year_axis <- .make_year_axis(rem_years)
      
      rem_colors <- species_colors[rem_species]
      missing_cols <- is.na(rem_colors)
      
      if (any(missing_cols)) {
        missing_species <- rem_species[missing_cols]
        extra_cols <- grDevices::hcl.colors(
          length(species_colors) + length(missing_species),
          palette = "Dark 3"
        )
        rem_colors[missing_species] <- tail(extra_cols, length(missing_species))
      }
      
      rem_colors <- rem_colors[rem_species]
      
      density_plot <- .complete_species_years(
        density_data,
        species_list = rem_species,
        year_axis = rem_year_axis
      )
      
      density_plot <- .add_line_segments(density_plot, "estimate")
      
      if (length(rem_species) > 100) {
        
        p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
          density_plot,
          ggplot2::aes(
            x = .data$Year_plot,
            y = .data$estimate,
            group = .data$line_group,
            color = .data$scientificName
          )
        ) +
          ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1.1, na.rm = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE) +
          ggplot2::geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2.8, fill = "white", stroke = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE) +
          ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ scientificName, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
          .x_year_scale(rem_year_axis, expand_right = 0.05) +
          ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = rem_colors, drop = FALSE) +
          ggplot2::labs(
            x = "Survey Year",
            y = expression("Density (individuals / km"^2*")")
          ) +
          .facet_plot_theme()
        
        print(p)
        
        .caption_html(
          object$getFigureNumber(text = FALSE),
          paste0(
            "Trends in estimated REM-based population density for each study species in the ",
            group_label,
            " group across survey years. Species are shown in separate panels to improve readability.",
            .gap_caption_text(rem_year_axis)
          )
        )
        
      } else {
        
        label_density <- .latest_labels(density_plot, "estimate")
        
        p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
          density_plot,
          ggplot2::aes(
            x = .data$Year_plot,
            y = .data$estimate,
            group = .data$line_group,
            color = .data$scientificName
          )
        ) +
          ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
          ggplot2::geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3.4, fill = "white", stroke = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
          ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
            data = label_density,
            ggplot2::aes(label = .data$scientificName),
            size = 4.2,
            nudge_x = 0.45,
            hjust = 0,
            direction = "y",
            segment.color = "gray60",
            segment.size = 0.4,
            box.padding = 0.35,
            point.padding = 0.25,
            family = "",
            show.legend = FALSE,
            na.rm = TRUE
          ) +
          .x_year_scale(rem_year_axis, expand_right = 0.30) +
          ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = rem_colors, drop = FALSE) +
          ggplot2::labs(
            x = "Survey Year",
            y = expression("Density (individuals / km"^2*")")
          ) +
          .main_plot_theme()
        
        print(p)
        
        .caption_html(
          object$getFigureNumber(text = FALSE),
          paste0(
            "Trends in estimated REM-based population density for each study species in the ",
            group_label,
            " group across survey years.",
            .gap_caption_text(rem_year_axis)
          )
        )
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Population Density Estimation

Population density was estimated using the Random Encounter Model (REM) for species with sufficient data to support reliable parameter estimation (*Palencia et al., 2022*). All REM analyses were conducted using the [camtrapDensity](https://github.com/MarcusRowcliffe/camtrapDensity) R package. Because detectability may vary among species, habitat types, and camera models, these estimates should be interpreted with reference to the assumptions of the model. The estimated model parameters and derived density values are presented in the following sections. For consistency, all density estimates were calculated using parameter values averaged across sampling rounds.

### REM Model Parameters {.tabset}

The REM relies on three key parameters: movement speed, activity level, and day range. Movement speed represents the average distance travelled by an individual over time, whereas activity level reflects the proportion of time individuals are active and therefore available for detection by camera traps. Day range refers to the total distance an animal typically moves within a 24-hour period and is derived from movement speed and activity level (Rowcliffe et al., 2008; Rowcliffe et al., 2016). Together, these parameters underpin the REM density estimates presented in this section. The tabs below show species-specific estimates for each parameter.

```{r model_parameters_REM_parameters, echo=FALSE, results="asis", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=11, fig.height=6.5, out.width="100%", fig.align="center", dpi=150}


# Get REM estimates


if (!exists("estimates_rem") || !is.data.frame(estimates_rem)) {
  
  spn <- object$get_speciesNames(object$setting$focus_groups)
  spn <- unique(as.character(spn))
  spn <- spn[!is.na(spn) & nzchar(spn)]
  
  rem_list <- list()
  
  if (length(spn) > 0) {
    for (sp in spn) {
      tmp <- try(object$get_REM(sp), silent = TRUE)
      
      if (!inherits(tmp, "try-error") && !is.null(tmp) && length(tmp) > 0) {
        tmp_df <- try(dplyr::bind_rows(tmp), silent = TRUE)
        
        if (!inherits(tmp_df, "try-error") && is.data.frame(tmp_df) && nrow(tmp_df) > 0) {
          rem_list[[sp]] <- tmp_df
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  estimates_rem <- dplyr::bind_rows(rem_list)
}

# -------------------------
# Helper functions
# -------------------------

.make_species_colors <- function(species) {
  
  species <- unique(as.character(species))
  species <- species[!is.na(species) & nzchar(species)]
  n <- length(species)
  
  if (n == 0) {
    return(stats::setNames(character(0), character(0)))
  }
  
  base_cols <- object$reportObjectElements$color_palette
  
  if (!is.null(base_cols) && length(base_cols) >= n) {
    cols <- base_cols[seq_len(n)]
  } else {
    cols <- grDevices::hcl.colors(n, palette = "Dark 3")
  }
  
  stats::setNames(cols, species)
}

.caption_html <- function(fig_no, text) {
  cat(paste0(
    '\n\n<p style="font-size:16px; color:black; font-weight:normal; margin-top:10px;">',
    '<b>Figure ', fig_no, '.</b> ',
    '<i>', text, '</i>',
    '</p>\n\n'
  ))
}

.prepare_parameter_data <- function(data, metric_name, lower_bound = 0, upper_bound = NULL) {
  
  if (!is.data.frame(data) || nrow(data) == 0 || !"Metric" %in% names(data)) {
    return(data.frame())
  }
  
  out <- data |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$Metric == metric_name) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Year_numeric = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(.data$Year))),
      estimate = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data$estimate)),
      lcl95 = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data$lcl95)),
      ucl95 = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data$ucl95))
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data$scientificName),
      nzchar(as.character(.data$scientificName)),
      !is.na(.data$Year_numeric),
      is.finite(.data$estimate)
    ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$scientificName) |>
    dplyr::slice_min(order_by = .data$Year_numeric, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()
  
  if (nrow(out) == 0) {
    return(out)
  }
  
  out$estimate_plot <- pmax(lower_bound, out$estimate)
  out$lcl95_plot <- ifelse(is.finite(out$lcl95), pmax(lower_bound, out$lcl95), NA_real_)
  out$ucl95_plot <- ifelse(is.finite(out$ucl95), out$ucl95, NA_real_)
  
  if (!is.null(upper_bound)) {
    out$estimate_plot <- pmin(upper_bound, out$estimate_plot)
    out$ucl95_plot <- ifelse(is.finite(out$ucl95_plot), pmin(upper_bound, out$ucl95_plot), NA_real_)
  }
  
  out |>
    dplyr::arrange(.data$scientificName)
}

.plot_parameter <- function(data, y_label, caption_text, upper_bound = NULL) {
  
  if (!is.data.frame(data) || nrow(data) == 0) {
    cat("\n\nNo data are available for this REM parameter.\n\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  data$scientificName <- factor(data$scientificName, levels = data$scientificName)
  
  species_colors <- .make_species_colors(data$scientificName)
  
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = .data$scientificName,
      y = .data$estimate_plot,
      fill = .data$scientificName
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.75) +
    ggplot2::geom_errorbar(
      ggplot2::aes(
        ymin = .data$lcl95_plot,
        ymax = .data$ucl95_plot
      ),
      width = 0.2,
      linewidth = 0.6,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      x = "Species",
      y = y_label
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = species_colors) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", color = "black"),
      axis.title.y = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", color = "black"),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()
    )
  
  if (is.null(upper_bound)) {
    p <- p +
      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        limits = c(0, NA),
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
      )
  } else {
    p <- p +
      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        limits = c(0, upper_bound),
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
      )
  }
  
  print(p)
  
  .caption_html(
    object$getFigureNumber(text = FALSE),
    caption_text
  )
}

# -------------------------
# Plot REM model parameters
# -------------------------

if (is.data.frame(estimates_rem) && nrow(estimates_rem) > 0) {
  
  cat('\n#### Movement Speed {.unnumbered}\n\n')
  
  active_speed_data <- .prepare_parameter_data(
    estimates_rem,
    metric_name = "active_speed",
    lower_bound = 0
  )
  
  .plot_parameter(
    active_speed_data,
    y_label = "Active speed (km/h)",
    caption_text = "Estimated active movement speeds (km/h) across study species. Error bars show 95% confidence intervals."
  )
  
  cat('\n#### Activity Level {.unnumbered}\n\n')
  
  activity_data <- .prepare_parameter_data(
    estimates_rem,
    metric_name = "activity_level",
    lower_bound = 0,
    upper_bound = 1
  )
  
  .plot_parameter(
    activity_data,
    y_label = "Proportion of time active",
    caption_text = "Estimated activity levels, expressed as the proportion of the day active, for each study species. Error bars show 95% confidence intervals.",
    upper_bound = 1
  )
  
  cat('\n#### Day Range {.unnumbered}\n\n')
  
  overall_speed_data <- .prepare_parameter_data(
    estimates_rem,
    metric_name = "overall_speed",
    lower_bound = 0
  )
  
  .plot_parameter(
    overall_speed_data,
    y_label = "Day range (km)",
    caption_text = "Estimated day ranges for each study species, calculated as the product of movement speed and activity level scaled to a 24-hour period. Error bars show 95% confidence intervals."
  )
  
} else {
  
  cat("\n\nREM model parameters are not available for the selected species.\n\n")
}
```

### Population Density Estimates {.tabset}

The plots below show annual population density estimates for each study species, together with 95% confidence intervals. These estimates allow comparison of temporal variation in density across survey years.


```{r population_densities_population_density, echo=FALSE, results="asis", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

if (!exists("estimates_rem") || is.null(estimates_rem)) {
  
  spn <- object$get_speciesNames(object$setting$focus_groups)
  spn <- unique(spn[!is.na(spn) & nzchar(spn)])
  
  rem_list <- list()
  
  if (length(spn) > 0) {
    for (sp in spn) {
      tmp <- try(object$get_REM(sp), silent = TRUE)
      
      if (!inherits(tmp, "try-error") && !is.null(tmp) && length(tmp) > 0) {
        tmp_df <- try(dplyr::bind_rows(tmp), silent = TRUE)
        
        if (!inherits(tmp_df, "try-error") && is.data.frame(tmp_df) && nrow(tmp_df) > 0) {
          rem_list[[sp]] <- tmp_df
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  estimates_rem <- dplyr::bind_rows(rem_list)
}

if (exists("estimates_rem") && !is.null(estimates_rem) && nrow(estimates_rem) > 0) {
  
  density_data <- estimates_rem |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$Metric == "density") |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data$scientificName)) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data$Year)) |>
    dplyr::filter(as.character(.data$Year) != "9999") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Year = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(.data$Year))),
      estimate = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data$estimate)),
      lcl95 = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data$lcl95)),
      ucl95 = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data$ucl95))
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(
      is.finite(.data$Year),
      is.finite(.data$estimate)
    )
  
  if (nrow(density_data) > 0) {
    
    species_list <- unique(density_data$scientificName)
    
    species_colors <- stats::setNames(
      rep(object$reportObjectElements$color_palette, length.out = length(species_list)),
      species_list
    )
    
    for (i in seq_along(species_list)) {
      
      species <- species_list[i]
      
      cat(paste0("\n#### ", species, " {.unnumbered}\n\n"))
      
      species_data <- density_data |>
        dplyr::filter(.data$scientificName == species) |>
        dplyr::arrange(.data$Year)
      
      if (nrow(species_data) == 0) {
        cat("\nNo REM density estimates were available for this species.\n\n")
        next
      }
      
      species_color <- species_colors[[species]]
      
      finite_est <- species_data$estimate[is.finite(species_data$estimate)]
      finite_ucl <- species_data$ucl95[is.finite(species_data$ucl95)]
      
      max_est <- max(finite_est, na.rm = TRUE)
      max_ucl <- if (length(finite_ucl) > 0) {
        max(finite_ucl, na.rm = TRUE)
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
      
      unstable_ci <- is.finite(max_ucl) &&
        is.finite(max_est) &&
        max_est > 0 &&
        max_ucl > 5 * max_est
      
      if (unstable_ci) {
        y_upper <- max_est * 1.6
      } else {
        y_upper <- max(c(species_data$estimate, species_data$ucl95), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.08
      }
      
      if (!is.finite(y_upper) || y_upper <= 0) {
        y_upper <- max(species_data$estimate, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.2
      }
      
      species_data <- species_data |>
        dplyr::mutate(
          lcl95_plot = dplyr::if_else(
            is.finite(.data$lcl95),
            pmax(.data$lcl95, 0),
            NA_real_
          ),
          ucl95_plot = dplyr::if_else(
            is.finite(.data$ucl95),
            pmin(.data$ucl95, y_upper),
            NA_real_
          ),
          ci_clipped = is.finite(.data$ucl95) & .data$ucl95 > y_upper
        )
      
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
        species_data,
        ggplot2::aes(
          x = factor(.data$Year),
          y = .data$estimate
        )
      ) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(
          fill = species_color,
          width = 0.6
        )
      
      if (any(is.finite(species_data$lcl95_plot)) && any(is.finite(species_data$ucl95_plot))) {
        p <- p +
          ggplot2::geom_errorbar(
            ggplot2::aes(
              ymin = .data$lcl95_plot,
              ymax = .data$ucl95_plot
            ),
            width = 0.18,
            color = "black",
            linewidth = 0.7,
            na.rm = TRUE
          )
      }
      
      if (any(species_data$ci_clipped, na.rm = TRUE)) {
        
        clipped_data <- species_data |>
          dplyr::filter(.data$ci_clipped)
        
        p <- p +
          ggplot2::geom_text(
            data = clipped_data,
            ggplot2::aes(
              x = factor(.data$Year),
              y = y_upper,
              label = "↑"
            ),
            inherit.aes = FALSE,
            size = 5,
            vjust = 1.1,
            color = "black"
          )
      }
      
      p <- p +
        ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
          ylim = c(0, y_upper),
          clip = "off"
        ) +
        ggplot2::labs(
          x = "Year",
          y = expression("Population density (km"^-2*")")
        ) +
        ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
        ggplot2::theme(
          axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", color = "black"),
          axis.title.y = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", color = "black"),
          plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
          panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()
        )
      
      print(p)
      
      if (unstable_ci) {
        cat(paste0(
          "\n\n*Note: The confidence intervals for **", species,
          "** are extremely wide relative to the point estimates. ",
          "The y-axis has been restricted for readability. Upward arrows indicate confidence intervals that extend beyond the displayed range. ",
          "This indicates high uncertainty in the REM estimate and should be interpreted cautiously.*\n"
        ))
      }
      
      cat(
        "\n\n",
        object$getFigureNumber(),
        " *Estimated population density per sampling year for ",
        species,
        ". Whiskers represent the 95% confidence intervals",
        if (unstable_ci) "; upward arrows indicate confidence intervals extending beyond the displayed y-axis range" else "",
        ".*\n\n",
        sep = ""
      )
    }
  }
}
```

## Activity Patterns {.tabset}

Activity patterns describe the temporal distribution of animal activity across the 24-hour day and are typically inferred from the timing of camera-trap detections. These patterns help identify whether species are primarily diurnal, nocturnal, or crepuscular, and can provide insight into daily behavior, ecological roles, and potential responses to environmental factors or human disturbance. The figures below present estimated daily activity curves for each study species, based on camera-trap detections collected across the monitoring period and derived using functionality from the [activity](https://cran.r-project.org/package=activity) R package (*Rowcliffe, 2016*).

```{r activity_patterns_activity_pattern, echo=FALSE, results="asis", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

if (!requireNamespace("activity", quietly = TRUE)) {
  
  cat("\n\nThe activity package is not installed; activity patterns cannot be estimated.\n")
  
} else if (!is.null(object$sun_times) && nrow(object$sun_times) > 0) {
  
  frequent_species_scientific <- object$get_speciesNames(object$setting$focus_groups)
  frequent_species_scientific <- unique(frequent_species_scientific)
  frequent_species_scientific <- frequent_species_scientific[!is.na(frequent_species_scientific)]
  
  # Color palette
  species_colors <- setNames(
    rep(object$reportObjectElements$color_palette, length.out = length(frequent_species_scientific)),
    frequent_species_scientific
  )
  
  # Compute total average sunrise/sunset
  overall_sunrise <- mean(object$sun_times$avg_sunrise, na.rm = TRUE)
  overall_sunset  <- mean(object$sun_times$avg_sunset,  na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Helper: create activity model directly from timestamps
  .fit_activity_direct <- function(object, species, reps = 10, min_records = 20) {
    
    dat <- object$data$observations
    
    if (is.null(dat) || !is.data.frame(dat) || nrow(dat) == 0) {
      stop("no observation data are available")
    }
    
    if (!all(c("scientificName", "timestamp") %in% names(dat))) {
      stop("scientificName or timestamp column is missing")
    }
    
    dat_sp <- dat |>
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(scientificName),
        scientificName == species,
        !is.na(timestamp)
      )
    
    if (nrow(dat_sp) == 0) {
      stop("no timestamped detections are available")
    }
    
    # Use one record per independent event where possible.
    # This avoids problems caused by count values and prevents over-weighting burst records.
    if ("sequenceID" %in% names(dat_sp) && any(!is.na(dat_sp$sequenceID))) {
      dat_sp <- dat_sp |>
        dplyr::filter(!is.na(sequenceID)) |>
        dplyr::distinct(sequenceID, .keep_all = TRUE)
    } else if ("observationID" %in% names(dat_sp) && any(!is.na(dat_sp$observationID))) {
      dat_sp <- dat_sp |>
        dplyr::filter(!is.na(observationID)) |>
        dplyr::distinct(observationID, .keep_all = TRUE)
    } else if ("deploymentID" %in% names(dat_sp)) {
      dat_sp <- dat_sp |>
        dplyr::distinct(deploymentID, timestamp, .keep_all = TRUE)
    } else {
      dat_sp <- dat_sp |>
        dplyr::distinct(timestamp, .keep_all = TRUE)
    }
    
    if (!inherits(dat_sp$timestamp, "POSIXct")) {
      tz_use <- "UTC"
      if (!is.null(object$setting$tz) && length(object$setting$tz) > 0 &&
          !is.na(object$setting$tz[1]) && nzchar(object$setting$tz[1])) {
        tz_use <- object$setting$tz[1]
      }
      dat_sp$timestamp <- as.POSIXct(dat_sp$timestamp, tz = tz_use)
    }
    
    dat_sp <- dat_sp[!is.na(dat_sp$timestamp), , drop = FALSE]
    
    # Convert clock time to radians, as required by activity::fitact()
    tt <- as.POSIXlt(dat_sp$timestamp)
    time_decimal <- tt$hour + tt$min / 60 + tt$sec / 3600
    time_rad <- (time_decimal / 24) * 2 * pi
    time_rad <- time_rad[is.finite(time_rad)]
    
    if (length(time_rad) < min_records) {
      stop(paste0("too few independent detections; n = ", length(time_rad)))
    }
    
    if (length(unique(round(time_rad, 6))) < 5) {
      stop("too few unique detection times")
    }
    
    activity::fitact(
      dat = time_rad,
      sample = "data",
      reps = reps,
      show = FALSE
    )
  }
  
  # Loop through species
  for (species in frequent_species_scientific) {
    
    cat("\n###", species, "{.unnumbered}\n\n")
    
    activity_model <- tryCatch(
      .fit_activity_direct(object, species = species, reps = 10, min_records = 20),
      error = function(e) e
    )
    
    if (inherits(activity_model, "error")) {
      
      cat(
        "\nActivity pattern could not be estimated for **",
        species,
        "**. Reason: ",
        activity_model$message,
        "\n\n",
        sep = ""
      )
      
    } else {
      
      pdf_obj <- activity_model@pdf
      
      # activity::fitact usually returns columns x, y, se, lcl, ucl.
      # This fallback also works if column names are missing.
      if (is.null(colnames(pdf_obj))) {
        colnames(pdf_obj) <- c("x", "y", "se", "lcl", "ucl")[seq_len(ncol(pdf_obj))]
      }
      
      activity_pred <- data.frame(
        time = (pdf_obj[, "x"] / (2 * pi)) * 24,
        estimate = pdf_obj[, "y"],
        lcl = if ("lcl" %in% colnames(pdf_obj)) pdf_obj[, "lcl"] else NA_real_,
        ucl = if ("ucl" %in% colnames(pdf_obj)) pdf_obj[, "ucl"] else NA_real_
      )
      
      activity_pred <- activity_pred[order(activity_pred$time), ]
      
      p <- ggplot(activity_pred, aes(x = time, y = estimate)) +
        geom_line(color = species_colors[[species]], linewidth = 1.2)
      
      if (any(is.finite(activity_pred$lcl)) && any(is.finite(activity_pred$ucl))) {
        p <- p +
          geom_ribbon(
            aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl),
            fill = species_colors[[species]],
            alpha = 0.3
          )
      }
      
      p <- p +
        geom_vline(xintercept = overall_sunrise, color = "gold", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
        geom_vline(xintercept = overall_sunset, color = "gray", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
        scale_x_continuous(
          limits = c(0, 24),
          breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 6),
          labels = c("00:00", "06:00", "12:00", "18:00", "24:00")
        ) +
        labs(
          x = "Time of Day",
          y = "Estimated Activity Density"
        ) +
        theme_minimal(base_family = "", base_size = 13) +
        theme(
          axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black"),
          axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
          legend.position = "none",
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(20, 40, 20, 40)
        )
      
      print(p)
      
      cat(paste0(
        "\n\n", object$getFigureNumber(),
        " *Estimated daily activity pattern for ",
        species,
        ", aggregated across all sampling rounds. Dashed lines indicate the average sunrise (yellow) and sunset (gray) times across survey years. The solid line shows the fitted activity model"
      ))
      
      if (any(is.finite(activity_pred$lcl)) && any(is.finite(activity_pred$ucl))) {
        cat(", and the shaded region shows the 95% CI")
      }
      
      cat(".*\n\n")
    }
  }
  
} else {
  cat('\n\nThe sun times have not been calculated; it requires the suncalc package. Please run setup first.\n')
}
```

## Richness {.tabset}

Species richness refers to the number of unique species recorded at each camera-trap location. It provides a useful indicator of local biodiversity and helps assess how effectively the survey captured variation in the wildlife community across the study area. The figure below shows the spatial distribution of species richness, where each point represents a camera-trap location. Circle size reflects the number of unique species detected at that site, and color indicates richness intensity, with warmer colors representing higher richness values. By selecting a point, users can view additional information on species composition, richness count, and habitat type, if available. These features help identify biodiversity hotspots and potential detection gaps across the study area.

```{r richness_Richness, echo=FALSE, results="asis", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.show="hold"}

study_areaSHP <- NULL

if (!is.null(object$study_area) && !is.null(object$study_area$path)) {
  object$study_area$object <- readRDS(object$study_area$path)
  study_areaSHP <- terra::project(object$study_area$object, "epsg:4326")
}

.richness_caption <- function(label) {
  cat(
    "\n\n",
    object$getFigureNumber(),
    " *Species richness based on the species focus group in this report, across camera-trap locations for ",
    label,
    ".*\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )
}

plot_richness <- function(data) {
  
  if (is.null(data) || !is.data.frame(data) || nrow(data) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  if (!all(c("longitude", "latitude", "Richness") %in% names(data))) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  data <- data |>
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data$longitude),
      !is.na(.data$latitude),
      !is.na(.data$Richness)
    )
  
  if (nrow(data) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  if (!"locationName" %in% names(data)) {
    data$locationName <- NA_character_
  }
  
  if (!"Community_Composition" %in% names(data)) {
    data$Community_Composition <- NA_character_
  }
  
  if (!"Habitat_Type" %in% names(data)) {
    data$Habitat_Type <- NA_character_
  }
  
  data <- data |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Habitat_Type = gsub("_", " ", as.character(.data$Habitat_Type)),
      popup = paste0(
        "<b>Location:</b> ", ifelse(!is.na(.data$locationName), .data$locationName, "N/A"), "<br>",
        "<b>Richness:</b> ", ifelse(!is.na(.data$Richness), .data$Richness, "N/A"), "<br>",
        "<b>Community:</b> ", ifelse(!is.na(.data$Community_Composition), .data$Community_Composition, "N/A"), "<br>",
        "<b>Habitat:</b> ", ifelse(!is.na(.data$Habitat_Type), .data$Habitat_Type, "N/A")
      )
    )
  
  data$Richness_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(data$Richness)))
  
  present_levels_num <- sort(unique(data$Richness_num[!is.na(data$Richness_num)]))
  present_levels <- as.character(present_levels_num)
  
  if (length(present_levels) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  full_palette <- object$reportObjectElements$richness_palette
  
  if (is.null(full_palette) || length(full_palette) == 0) {
    full_palette <- grDevices::hcl.colors(length(present_levels), palette = "YlOrRd")
  }
  
  richness_cols <- rep(full_palette, length.out = length(present_levels))
  
  data$Richness <- factor(
    as.character(data$Richness_num),
    levels = present_levels,
    ordered = TRUE
  )
  
  legend_values <- factor(
    present_levels,
    levels = present_levels,
    ordered = TRUE
  )
  
  richness_palette <- leaflet::colorFactor(
    palette = richness_cols,
    domain = legend_values,
    ordered = TRUE,
    na.color = "#bdbdbd"
  )
  
  map <- leaflet::leaflet(data) |>
    leaflet::addTiles() |>
    leaflet::addCircleMarkers(
      lng = ~longitude,
      lat = ~latitude,
      radius = ~ifelse(
        is.na(Richness_num),
        2,
        ifelse(Richness_num == 1, 2, Richness_num * 2)
      ),
      fillColor = ~richness_palette(Richness),
      fillOpacity = 0.7,
      stroke = TRUE,
      color = "black",
      weight = 1,
      popup = ~popup
    )
  
  if (!is.null(study_areaSHP)) {
    map <- map |>
      leaflet::addPolygons(
        data = study_areaSHP,
        color = "#3A3F44",
        weight = 2,
        opacity = 0.9,
        fillColor = "transparent",
        fillOpacity = 0,
        options = leaflet::pathOptions(interactive = FALSE)
      )
  }
  
  lon_range <- range(data$longitude, na.rm = TRUE)
  lat_range <- range(data$latitude, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  if (all(is.finite(lon_range)) && all(is.finite(lat_range))) {
    map <- map |>
      leaflet::fitBounds(
        lng1 = lon_range[1],
        lat1 = lat_range[1],
        lng2 = lon_range[2],
        lat2 = lat_range[2]
      )
  }
  
  map <- map |>
    leaflet::addLegend(
      position = "bottomright",
      pal = richness_palette,
      values = legend_values,
      title = "Species Richness",
      opacity = 1,
      labFormat = leaflet::labelFormat(transform = function(x) as.character(x))
    )
  
  map
}

# -------------------------
# Richness maps by year
# -------------------------

for (.year in object$years) {
  
  cat(paste0("\n### ", .year, " {.unnumbered}\n\n"))
  
  .richness <- object$richness(
    year = .year,
    spList = object$get_speciesNames(group = object$setting$focus_groups)
  )
  
  p <- plot_richness(.richness)
  
  if (is.null(p)) {
    cat(paste0("\nNo richness map could be generated for ", .year, ".\n\n"))
  } else {
    print(htmltools::tagList(p))
    .richness_caption(paste0("survey year ", .year))
  }
}

# -------------------------
# Total richness map
# -------------------------

cat("\n\n### Total {.unnumbered}\n\n")

.richness <- object$richness(
  year = NULL,
  spList = object$get_speciesNames(group = object$setting$focus_groups)
)

p <- plot_richness(.richness)

if (is.null(p)) {
  cat("\nNo cumulative richness map could be generated.\n\n")
} else {
  print(htmltools::tagList(p))
  .richness_caption("the cumulative dataset across all years")
}
```

## Species Co-occurrence {.tabset}

Species co-occurrence analysis was used to assess pairwise associations among species recorded across camera-trap locations. Relationships were summarized in a correlation matrix, where positive values indicate species pairs that tended to co-occur more frequently across sites and negative values indicate lower co-occurrence. Such patterns can provide insight into shared space use or spatial segregation among species, although they should be interpreted cautiously because co-occurrence alone does not imply direct interaction. (*Gotelli, 2000*).

```{r co_occurrence_co_occurrence, echo=FALSE, results="asis", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, cache=FALSE}

.spn <- object$get_speciesNames(object$setting$focus_groups)

.pa <- FALSE
if (!is.null(object$setting$PA) && is.logical(object$setting$PA)) {
  .pa <- object$setting$PA
}

.valid_cor_matrix <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) return(FALSE)
  if (!(is.matrix(x) || is.data.frame(x))) return(FALSE)
  if (length(x) == 0) return(FALSE)
  if (all(is.na(x))) return(FALSE)
  TRUE
}

.plot_cooccurrence <- function(.spo, .title) {
  
  if (.require("corrplot")) {
    
    corrplot::corrplot(
      as.matrix(.spo),
      method = "color",
      type = "upper",
      order = "hclust",
      tl.col = "black",
      tl.srt = 45,
      tl.cex = 0.8,
      diag = FALSE,
      title = .title,
      mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0)
    )
    
  } else {
    
    par(mar = c(7, 8, 4, 4))
    .basic_corrplot(as.matrix(.spo), main = .title)
  }
}

.co_caption <- function(label) {
  cat(
    "\n\n",
    object$getFigureNumber(),
    " *Species co-occurrence patterns for the selected species focus group in this report, shown for ",
    label,
    ".*\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )
}

# -------------------------
# Year-specific co-occurrence
# -------------------------

for (.year in object$years) {
  
  .spo <- object$species_summary_by_location(
    year = .year,
    spList = .spn,
    cor_matrix = TRUE,
    PA = .pa
  )
  
  if (.valid_cor_matrix(.spo)) {
    
    cat(paste0("\n### ", .year, " {.unnumbered}\n\n"))
    
    .plot_cooccurrence(
      .spo = .spo,
      .title = paste0("Species Co-occurrence (Year: ", .year, ")")
    )
    
    .co_caption(paste0("survey year ", .year))
  }
}

# -------------------------
# Total co-occurrence
# -------------------------

.spo <- object$species_summary_by_location(
  spList = .spn,
  cor_matrix = TRUE,
  PA = .pa
)

if (.valid_cor_matrix(.spo)) {
  
  cat("\n### Total {.unnumbered}\n\n")
  
  .plot_cooccurrence(
    .spo = .spo,
    .title = "Species Co-occurrence (Total)"
  )
  
  .co_caption("the cumulative dataset across all years")
}
```

## Spatial Density {.tabset}

Spatial density maps derived from point pattern analysis illustrate the spatial distribution of species detections across the study area. These visualizations highlight variation in detection intensity and help identify areas with relatively high or low concentrations of records. The following maps are presented for each species, either by survey year or across the full monitoring period. Warmer colors represent higher estimated detection density, whereas cooler colors indicate lower density. Together, these maps support comparison of spatial detection patterns among species and across survey years.

```{r spatial_density_spatial_density, echo=FALSE, results="asis", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

.spn <- object$get_speciesNames(object$setting$focus_groups)

df_all <- object$species_summary_by_location(
  year = NULL,
  spList = .spn,
  cor_matrix = FALSE
)

if (is.null(df_all) || nrow(df_all) == 0) {
  
  cat("\n\nNo spatial density data were available for the selected species focus group.\n\n")
  
} else {
  
  df_all$lon <- df_all$longitude
  df_all$lat <- df_all$latitude
  
  .dfs_all <- terra::vect(
    df_all,
    geom = c("lon", "lat"),
    crs = terra::crs(terra::rast())
  )
  
  .dfs_all <- .get_projected_vect(.dfs_all)
  .crs <- terra::crs(.dfs_all)
  
  if (!is.null(object$study_area) && !is.null(object$study_area$path)) {
    object$study_area$object <- terra::readRDS(object$study_area$path)
    .crop <- terra::project(object$study_area$object, .crs)
    .ext <- as.vector(terra::ext(.crop))
  } else {
    .crop <- NULL
    .ext <- NULL
  }
  
  .density_caption <- function(sp, label) {
    cat(
      "\n\n",
      object$getFigureNumber(),
      " *Spatial point pattern density for **",
      sp,
      "** based on the species focus group in this report, shown for ",
      label,
      ".*\n\n",
      sep = ""
    )
  }
  
  .generate_density_maps <- function(.year = NULL, .ext = .ext, .crop = .crop) {
    
    df <- object$species_summary_by_location(
      year = .year,
      spList = .spn,
      cor_matrix = FALSE
    )
    
    if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    
    df <- df |>
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(.data$longitude),
        !is.na(.data$latitude)
      )
    
    if (nrow(df) == 0) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    
    df$lon <- df$longitude
    df$lat <- df$latitude
    
    .dfs <- terra::vect(
      df,
      geom = c("lon", "lat"),
      crs = terra::crs(terra::rast())
    )
    
    .dfs <- .get_projected_vect(.dfs)
    .crs_local <- terra::crs(.dfs)
    .dfs <- as.data.frame(.dfs, geom = "XY")
    
    .w <- table(.dfs$scientificName)
    .w <- .w[.w > 3]
    
    if (length(.w) == 0) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    
    species_list <- names(.w)
    
    .label <- "Total"
    .caption_label <- "the cumulative dataset across all years"
    
    if (!is.null(.year)) {
      .label <- as.character(.year)
      .caption_label <- paste0("survey year ", .year)
    }
    
    cat("\n### ", .label, " {.tabset .unnumbered}\n\n", sep = "")
    
    for (sp in species_list) {
      
      df_sp <- .dfs |>
        dplyr::filter(.data$scientificName == sp)
      
      if (nrow(df_sp) < 4) {
        next
      }
      
      r <- try(
        object$spatial_density(
          df_sp,
          .crs = .crs_local,
          .ext = .ext,
          .crop = .crop
        ),
        silent = TRUE
      )
      
      if (inherits(r, "try-error") || is.null(r)) {
        next
      }
      
      cat("\n#### ", sp, " {.unnumbered}\n\n", sep = "")
      
      m <- leaflet::leaflet(df_sp) |>
        leaflet::addTiles(group = "OSM") |>
        leaflet::addRasterImage(
          r,
          opacity = 0.7,
          colors = grDevices::colorRampPalette(
            c("gray", "orange", "red", "darkred")
          )(200),
          group = "Density"
        )
      
      if ("Habitat_type" %in% colnames(df_sp)) {
        
        m <- m |>
          leaflet::addCircleMarkers(
            ~longitude,
            ~latitude,
            popup = ~sprintf(
              "<b>%s</b><br/>%s<br/>Obs: %d<br/>Habitat: %s",
              scientificName,
              locationName,
              total_observations,
              Habitat_type
            ),
            radius = ~sqrt(total_observations) * 1.2,
            color = "blue",
            fillOpacity = 0.4,
            group = "Points"
          )
        
      } else {
        
        m <- m |>
          leaflet::addCircleMarkers(
            ~longitude,
            ~latitude,
            popup = ~sprintf(
              "<b>%s</b><br/>%s<br/>Obs: %d",
              scientificName,
              locationName,
              total_observations
            ),
            radius = ~sqrt(total_observations) * 1.2,
            color = "blue",
            fillOpacity = 0.4,
            group = "Points"
          )
      }
      
      if (!is.null(.crop)) {
        m <- m |>
          leaflet::addPolygons(
            data = terra::project(.crop, "epsg:4326"),
            fillColor = "transparent",
            fillOpacity = 0.3,
            color = "black",
            weight = 2,
            options = leaflet::pathOptions(interactive = FALSE)
          )
      }
      
      m <- m |>
        leaflet::addLayersControl(
          baseGroups = "OSM",
          overlayGroups = c("Density", "Points"),
          options = leaflet::layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
        ) |>
        leaflet::setView(
          lng = mean(df_sp$longitude, na.rm = TRUE),
          lat = mean(df_sp$latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
          zoom = 11
        )
      
      print(htmltools::tagList(m))
      
      .density_caption(sp, .caption_label)
    }
  }
  
  for (.year in object$years) {
    .generate_density_maps(.year = .year, .ext = .ext, .crop = .crop)
  }
  
  .generate_density_maps(.year = NULL, .ext = .ext, .crop = .crop)
}
```

## Habitat Preferences {.tabset}

Habitat preferences were assessed by comparing proportional capture rates across habitat types for each species. Capture rate, expressed as detections relative to sampling effort, serves here as an indicator of habitat use and relative habitat association rather than a direct estimate of habitat selection. Differences in the distribution of capture rates among habitat types therefore highlight habitats in which species were more or less frequently recorded. Together, these patterns provide insight into species-specific habitat use within the study area and help identify broad differences in habitat association among the focal species.

```{r habitat_preferences_habitat_selection, echo=FALSE, results="asis", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}


.spn <- object$get_speciesNames(object$setting$focus_groups)

capture_habitat_sel <- object$species_summary_by_habitat

if (!is.null(capture_habitat_sel) && nrow(capture_habitat_sel) > 0) {
  
  capture_habitat_sel <- capture_habitat_sel |>
    dplyr::filter(scientificName %in% .spn)
  
  if (nrow(capture_habitat_sel) > 0) {
    
    # Define Acadia color palette
    acadia_colors <- object$reportObjectElements$acadia_colors
    
    # Create a color mapping for habitat types
    habitat_types <- unique(capture_habitat_sel$Habitat_Type)
    habitat_colors <- stats::setNames(
      rep(acadia_colors, length.out = length(habitat_types)),
      habitat_types
    )
    
    # Generate the plot
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
      capture_habitat_sel,

}
```
